butternut-squash-jus.name: butternut squash jus with brown sugar and brown butter

cocktails.name: Absinthe Frappé
cocktails.notes: The New Orleans tourism board’s mint version; fold in the soda gently.

cocktails.name: Air Mail
cocktails.notes: Bacardí’s aged-rum and prosecco version, using the house 3:1 honey syrup; add the wine after straining.

cocktails.name: Algonquin
cocktails.notes: Hess’s hotel spec is stirred to keep the pineapple juice from foaming.

cocktails.name: Amaretto Sour
cocktails.notes: Jeffrey Morgenthaler’s bourbon-strengthened version.

cocktails.name: Ancient Mariner
cocktails.notes: Difford’s adaptation of Jeff “Beachbum” Berry’s drink.

cocktails.name: Army & Navy
cocktails.notes: Embury ran it drier; this is the common modern balance.

cocktails.name: Art of Choke
cocktails.notes: Kyle Davidson’s spec uses only ¾ teaspoon each of lime juice and rich demerara syrup.

cocktails.name: Artichoke Hold
cocktails.notes: Jeremy Oertel’s Donna spec uses lime juice and Jamaican rum.

cocktails.name: B & B
cocktails.notes: Traditional equal parts, served at room temperature.

cocktails.name: Bamboo
cocktails.notes: Credited to Louis Eppinger at the Grand Hotel, Yokohama, in the 1890s.

cocktails.name: Barbacoa
cocktails.garnish: red bell pepper strip and beef jerky
cocktails.notes: Julian Cox’s Saveur spec: muddle the lime and modifiers, then add mezcal and ice and transfer the whole drink to the serving glass.

cocktails.name: Batanga
cocktails.notes: At La Capilla in Tequila, Don Javier stirs it with the knife he cut the lime with.

cocktails.name: Batida de Maracujá
cocktails.notes: Swap the passion fruit for coconut or other fruit for the other batidas.

cocktails.name: Benton's Old Fashioned
cocktails.notes: Don Lee’s PDT spec, served without ice. For the bourbon, combine 45 g melted Benton’s bacon fat with 750 ml bourbon, rest four hours, freeze two hours, then remove the fat and filter.

cocktails.name: Betsy Ross
cocktails.notes: Difford’s equal-parts brandy and tawny port version.

cocktails.name: Bitter Giuseppe
cocktails.notes: Stephen Cole, The Violet Hour. The original is stirred despite its lemon juice.

cocktails.name: Black Manhattan
cocktails.notes: Averna replaces sweet vermouth in Todd Smith’s Manhattan variation.

cocktails.name: Blinker
cocktails.notes: Jeff Knott’s grenadine version; Ted Haigh’s revival spec uses raspberry syrup instead.

cocktails.name: Blue Hawaii
cocktails.notes: Harry Yee’s 1957 spec; lemon and syrup replace his sweet-and-sour mix.

cocktails.name: Boulevardier
cocktails.notes: Equal parts is the original; the extra whiskey keeps it from getting syrupy.

cocktails.name: Bourbon Renewal
cocktails.notes: Jeffrey Morgenthaler’s original published spec.

cocktails.name: Brandy Crusta
cocktails.garnish: sugar rim and long lemon peel

cocktails.name: Brandy Daisy
cocktails.notes: Thomas finishes it with just a splash of seltzer.

cocktails.name: Breakfast Martini
cocktails.notes: Salvatore Calabrese’s marmalade sour.

cocktails.name: Brooklyn
cocktails.notes: Today’s export Amer Picon is weaker than the original; Bigallet China-China is the usual stand-in.

cocktails.name: Buck's Fizz
cocktails.notes: Two parts Champagne to one part orange juice.

cocktails.name: Butternut & Falernum
cocktails.notes: Eben Freeman’s Tailor spec uses Matusalem Gran Reserva and Velvet Falernum. For the jus, reduce 480 ml freshly juiced butternut squash by one third, dissolve 5 tablespoons brown sugar, add 5 tablespoons brown butter, refrigerate overnight, then sieve out the butter solids.

cocktails.name: Canchanchara
cocktails.notes: Dissolve the honey in the water and lime juice before adding ice and aguardiente.

cocktails.name: Carajillo
cocktails.notes: The Mexican shaken style; in Spain it’s brandy or rum stirred into hot coffee.

cocktails.name: Champagne Cocktail
cocktails.notes: IBA allows a few drops of Grand Marnier as an optional addition.

cocktails.name: Champs-Élysées
cocktails.notes: Difford’s modern proportions, with green Chartreuse and rich syrup; saline omitted.

cocktails.name: Chet Baker
cocktails.notes: Sam Ross’s dry proportions, using the house 3:1 honey syrup.

cocktails.name: Closing Argument
cocktails.notes: A Last Word with mezcal in place of gin; also known as the Mezcal Last Word.

cocktails.name: Cock N’ Bull Special
cocktails.notes: Saucier’s 1951 spec uses Cointreau and no bitters.

cocktails.name: De La Louisiane
cocktails.notes: Arthur’s 1937 equal-parts spec; many bars now double the rye.

cocktails.name: Death in the Afternoon
cocktails.notes: Hemingway: add iced Champagne until it attains the proper opalescent milkiness.

cocktails.name: Division Bell
cocktails.notes: Phil Ward’s mezcal riff on the Last Word.

cocktails.name: Earl Grey MarTEAni
cocktails.garnish: half sugar rim and lemon twist
cocktails.notes: Infuse the gin with loose Earl Grey for about two hours.

cocktails.name: El Diablo
cocktails.notes: Add the ginger beer after straining.

cocktails.name: El Presidente
cocktails.notes: Use a blanc (bianco) vermouth, not a French dry.

cocktails.name: Final Ward
cocktails.notes: Phil Ward’s rye-and-lemon variation on the Last Word.

cocktails.name: French 75
cocktails.notes: Cognac instead of gin is the other classic.

cocktails.name: French Maid
cocktails.notes: Difford’s adaptation of Jim Meehan’s drink; add ginger beer after straining.

cocktails.name: French Pearl
cocktails.notes: Audrey Saunders, Pegu Club. Muddle the mint with the lime and syrup; fine-strain.

cocktails.name: Gibson
cocktails.notes: A Dry Martini with an onion and no bitters.

cocktails.name: Gimlet
cocktails.notes: Fresh-lime version. For the original, use 22.5 ml lime cordial and stir.

cocktails.name: Gin Blossom
cocktails.notes: Julie Reiner’s spec uses unsweetened apricot eau de vie, rather than apricot liqueur.

cocktails.name: Gin Fizz
cocktails.notes: Serve without ice; add just a splash of soda.

cocktails.name: Gin-Gin Mule
cocktails.garnish: mint sprig, lime wheel and candied ginger
cocktails.notes: Audrey Saunders’ allowance for commercial ginger beer uses 15 ml syrup; her homemade version uses 30 ml. Add carbonated ginger beer after shaking.

cocktails.name: Godfather
cocktails.notes: The old IBA spec was equal parts; most bars now pour 2:1.

cocktails.name: Godmother
cocktails.notes: The Godfather with vodka.

cocktails.name: Golden Cadillac
cocktails.notes: From Poor Red’s in El Dorado, California, 1952.

cocktails.name: Halekulani
cocktails.notes: Bourbon version in Difford’s proportions; his adaptation of Shannon Mustipher’s spec substitutes rye.

cocktails.name: Harvey Wallbanger
cocktails.notes: Galliano’s published metric spec.

cocktails.name: Hemingway Daiquiri
cocktails.notes: No added sugar; it should be tart.

cocktails.name: Highball
cocktails.notes: The Scotch-and-soda version, at one part whisky to three parts soda.

cocktails.name: Hotel Georgia
cocktails.notes: The Hotel Georgia archive recipe, converted at 30 ml per ounce.

cocktails.name: Hotel Nacional
cocktails.notes: Bacardí’s aged-rum spec; earlier versions use white rum.

cocktails.name: Hurricane
cocktails.notes: Alton Brown’s large single serve of the three-ingredient New Orleans style, with bitters added in the glass.

cocktails.name: IBA Tiki
cocktails.notes: Muddle a thin slice of ginger before shaking.

cocktails.name: Illegal
cocktails.notes: IBA allows a few drops of egg white as an optional addition.

cocktails.name: Industry Sour
cocktails.notes: Ted Kilgore’s original equal-parts spec, without the egg white and saline of later versions.

cocktails.name: Intro to Aperol
cocktails.notes: Audrey Saunders’s Aperol-led sour.

cocktails.name: Irish Coffee
cocktails.notes: Warm the glass first. Cream poured over a spoon, not stirred in.

cocktails.name: Italian Greyhound
cocktails.notes: The vodka, Campari and grapefruit version.

cocktails.name: Jack Rose
cocktails.notes: Use a real pomegranate grenadine; it carries the drink.

cocktails.name: Jasmine
cocktails.notes: Paul Harrington’s original proportions.

cocktails.name: Jet Pilot
cocktails.notes: Flash-blend for a few seconds only.

cocktails.name: John Collins
cocktails.notes: Old Tom gin makes the Tom Collins variant.

cocktails.name: Journalist
cocktails.notes: The Savoy proportions, with just two dashes each of lemon and curaçao.

cocktails.name: Kangaroo
cocktails.notes: The vodka Martini, in 4:1 proportions.

cocktails.name: Kir Royale
cocktails.notes: The Kir with Champagne in place of white wine.

cocktails.name: Last Tango in Modena
cocktails.notes: Biancaniello’s Home & Family spec: muddle the strawberries with the vinegar and top the finished drink with foam. For the foam, charge 240 ml each St-Germain and egg whites in a siphon with two N2O cartridges and chill overnight.

cocktails.name: Last Word
cocktails.notes: Revived by Murray Stenson at Seattle’s Zig Zag Café in the early 2000s.

cocktails.name: Leap Year
cocktails.notes: Harry Craddock’s 1928 Savoy spec uses just a dash of lemon juice.

cocktails.name: Lion's Tail
cocktails.notes: Difford’s proportions use a restrained measure of allspice dram.

cocktails.name: Mai Tai
cocktails.garnish: mint sprig and spent lime shell

cocktails.name: Mamie Taylor
cocktails.notes: Named for the Broadway singer in 1899; the forerunner of the Moscow Mule.

cocktails.name: Mexican Firing Squad
cocktails.garnish: orange slice, pineapple wedge and cherry
cocktails.notes: Difford’s adaptation of Baker’s 1939 spec; serve without soda.

cocktails.name: Mezcalada
cocktails.garnish: salt, sugar and Tajín rim; lime wheel
cocktails.notes: Casamigos’s tomato-based mezcal Michelada, using plain ice in place of its serrano, dill and pickle-juice ice block; add the beer after straining.

cocktails.name: Milano-Torino
cocktails.notes: Campari from Milan, vermouth from Turin: the Americano before the soda.

cocktails.name: Milk Punch
cocktails.notes: The unclarified New Orleans brandy version, in a tall glass to fit the full cup of milk.

cocktails.name: Missionary's Downfall
cocktails.notes: Blend with half a cup of crushed ice.

cocktails.name: Morning Glory
cocktails.notes: The brandy-and-whiskey version, with Angostura as the aromatic bitters; add soda after straining.

cocktails.name: Napoleon
cocktails.notes: The Savoy version seasons a full measure of gin with a dash of each modifier.

cocktails.name: Navy Grog
cocktails.notes: Don’s 1941 spec; traditionally served around a shaved-ice cone with the straw through it.

cocktails.name: Negroni Sbagliato
cocktails.notes: Bar Basso’s “mistaken” Negroni, with sparkling wine where the gin should be.

cocktails.name: New York Sour
cocktails.notes: Float the red wine; rye or bourbon may be used.

cocktails.name: Nuclear Daiquiri
cocktails.notes: Gregor de Gruyther’s drink in Difford’s proportions; use wet ice and omit the source’s optional added water.

cocktails.name: Oaxaca Old Fashioned
cocktails.notes: Phil Ward, Death & Co, 2007. Use undiluted agave nectar.

cocktails.name: Old Cuban
cocktails.notes: Add the Champagne after straining.

cocktails.name: Old Fashioned
cocktails.notes: Rye works just as well; a sugar cube muddled with the bitters is the older form.

cocktails.name: Old Hickory
cocktails.notes: Stanley Clisby Arthur’s 1937 equal-parts vermouth spec.

cocktails.name: Painkiller
cocktails.notes: From the Soggy Dollar Bar on Jost Van Dyke in the 1970s; navy rum is the standard pour.

cocktails.name: Pendennis Club
cocktails.notes: Ted Haigh’s spec uses sweetened apricot brandy liqueur, rather than apricot eau de vie.

cocktails.name: Pimm's Cup
cocktails.garnish: orange slice, cucumber slice, strawberry and mint sprig
cocktails.notes: The British serve uses sparkling lemonade.

cocktails.name: Pink Lady
cocktails.notes: The gin-and-applejack version, using Steve the Bartender’s proportions.

cocktails.name: Pink Squirrel
cocktails.notes: From Bryant’s Cocktail Lounge in Milwaukee, which still blends it with ice cream.

cocktails.name: Pisco Punch
cocktails.notes: Muddle the cloves in the syrup; add the wine after double-straining.

cocktails.name: Planter's Punch
cocktails.notes: IBA leaves dilution to taste; this version uses ice.

cocktails.name: Porn Star Martini
cocktails.notes: Serve the Champagne separately alongside the cocktail.

cocktails.name: Queen’s Park Swizzle
cocktails.notes: From the Queen’s Park Hotel in Port of Spain, Trinidad; the bitters layer on top after swizzling.

cocktails.name: Rattlesnake
cocktails.garnish: Angostura bitters drawn through the foam
cocktails.notes: Difford’s modern spec uses rich syrup and three dashes of absinthe.

cocktails.name: Red Hook
cocktails.notes: Enzo Errico’s Milk & Honey spec with Punt e Mes; maraschino can be reduced to 7.5 ml.

cocktails.name: Remember the Maine
cocktails.notes: Use the absinthe to rinse the glass, then discard. Cherry Heering replaces the IBA-specified Luxardo cherry brandy.

cocktails.name: Revolver
cocktails.notes: Jon Santer’s bourbon-and-coffee riff, created at Bruno’s in San Francisco.

cocktails.name: Ritz Cocktail
cocktails.notes: Dale DeGroff’s spec; add the Champagne after straining.

cocktails.name: Rock and Rye
cocktails.notes: Thomas’s simple whiskey-and-syrup serve, measuring the wineglass as 60 ml and using rich simple syrup for rock-candy syrup.

cocktails.name: Rose Cocktail
cocktails.notes: Use kirsch eau de vie, rather than a sweet cherry liqueur.

cocktails.name: Royal Fizz
cocktails.notes: The Gin Fizz with a whole egg; dry-shake first.

cocktails.name: Salomé
cocktails.notes: The equal-parts gin, dry vermouth and Dubonnet version.

cocktails.name: Saratoga
cocktails.notes: The brandy-and-whiskey Saratoga, in equal parts with sweet vermouth.

cocktails.name: Satan’s Whiskers
cocktails.notes: The Savoy’s “straight” version; orange curaçao in place of Grand Marnier makes it “curled”.

cocktails.name: Saturn
cocktails.garnish: lemon peel ring around a cherry
cocktails.notes: J. “Popo” Galsini’s 1967 gin tiki drink.

cocktails.name: Sazerac
cocktails.notes: Served neat in a chilled glass. Half rye, half cognac is a good variation.

cocktails.name: Scofflaw
cocktails.notes: The 1924 Harry’s ABC proportions, using rye for the Canadian whiskey.

cocktails.name: Scorpion
cocktails.notes: The single-serve version of Vic’s communal Scorpion Bowl.

cocktails.name: Seelbach
cocktails.notes: Adam Seger launched it in 1995 as a lost 1912 house recipe and admitted in 2016 he made that up.

cocktails.name: Sherry Cobbler
cocktails.garnish: berries, orange and lemon quarter wheels
cocktails.notes: Use half a wheel each of orange and lemon, cut into quarters.

cocktails.name: Siesta
cocktails.notes: Katie Stipe’s tequila-and-Campari variation on the Hemingway Daiquiri.

cocktails.name: Silver Fizz
cocktails.notes: The Gin Fizz with egg white; a yolk instead makes a Golden Fizz.

cocktails.name: Singapore Sling
cocktails.notes: Cherry Heering replaces the IBA-specified Sangue Morlacco cherry liqueur.

cocktails.name: Southside
cocktails.notes: Lemon is also traditional; top with soda in a highball for a Southside Fizz.

cocktails.name: Spicy Fifty
cocktails.notes: Use thin chili slices; double-strain.

cocktails.name: Stork Club Cocktail
cocktails.notes: Beebe’s 1946 spec, measuring the juice of half an orange as 30 ml.

cocktails.name: Stout Flip
cocktails.notes: Steve the Bartender’s spiced-rum version; degas the stout before shaking.

cocktails.name: Suffering Bastard
cocktails.notes: Pour unstrained and finish with ginger beer.

cocktails.name: Three Dots and a Dash
cocktails.garnish: three cherries and a rectangular pineapple chunk

cocktails.name: Ti’ Punch
cocktails.notes: In Martinique the bottle, limes and syrup go on the table and each guest builds their own.

cocktails.name: Tom Collins
cocktails.notes: London dry makes a drier drink.

cocktails.name: Trident
cocktails.notes: Robert Hess’s updated recipe includes orange bitters alongside peach bitters.

cocktails.name: Twentieth Century
cocktails.notes: Named for the New York–Chicago train; Lillet stands in for the original Kina Lillet.

cocktails.name: Tía Mía
cocktails.notes: A split-base Mai Tai.

cocktails.name: Up to Date
cocktails.notes: Ensslin’s 1916 equal-parts whiskey and sherry spec, using amontillado.

cocktails.name: Ve.N.To
cocktails.notes: The honey mix may use chamomile infusion in place of water; egg white is optional.

cocktails.name: Vesper
cocktails.notes: IBA spec. Fleming's original is 90 ml gin, 30 ml vodka and 15 ml Kina Lillet.

cocktails.name: Vieux Mot
cocktails.notes: Difford’s adaptation of Don Lee’s PDT spec, with rich syrup.

cocktails.name: Whiskey Smash
cocktails.notes: DeGroff’s revival of the 1880s smash; double-strain over fresh crushed ice.

cocktails.name: White Russian
cocktails.notes: The Black Russian with cream on top.

cocktails.name: Widow's Kiss
cocktails.notes: Kappeler’s original 2:1:1 proportions, with yellow Chartreuse.

cocktails.name: Zombie
cocktails.notes: Flash blend for about five seconds with 180 ml crushed ice. Limit two per guest.
